title: A cube with per-face normals -- and this case decides its silhouette, not its faceting

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's azimuth 35 and elevation 20 put no silhouette edge of an axis-aligned cube on a raster row, column or diagonal. The subject's own point -- unsmoothed faces -- is NOT what this decides, and the acceptance says so rather than letting a green read as a claim about normals.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: Cube
subjects.notes: POSITION, NORMAL, TANGENT and TEXCOORD_0, with the corners split so each carries its face's normal. The file's baseColour texture is not read by this case.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-1.0, -1.0, -1.0] to [1.0, 1.0, 1.000001], so centre = [0.0, 0.0, 4.999999999588667e-07] and radius = 1.73205109624406 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 12.369693216177938, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius. QUOTED FROM THE RULE'S OWN OUTPUT, not recomputed beside it: the bounds are the AABB of the TRANSFORMED VERTICES, and an authoring helper that transformed the eight corners of the local AABB produced a looser box wherever a node rotates -- 7.464e-08 m of eye, five orders past the runner's tolerance.
camera.note: The glTF carries no camera, so the framing rule supplies one. Roll is 0 because the rule sets it: a roll chosen here and nowhere else would make this subject's placement a second determination competing with the rule.

light.note: The material below emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist. A light here would add a lobe neither side is being asked about.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest and not of a Blender default. At zero bounces an emission shader returns its emission alone, so this changes no covered pixel -- it removes the background from the DECLARATION rather than from the render.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material. UNDER A UNIFORM ENVIRONMENT AN UNOCCLUDED DIFFUSE FACE RETURNS rho*L INDEPENDENT OF ITS NORMAL, so a lit arm would render every face of a convex body the same colour and the faceting would be invisible by construction -- which is why this case does not pretend to decide it.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case for a solid. The model's criterion is faceting and it needs a shading arm that can separate two faces; that is board:1363's territory and it is not claimed here.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the projected area of the subject's triangles over the declared raster at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the subject's own vertices. Quoted because the boundary bound is applied UNDER it: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's apparent size, so a camera framing the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so.
subjectFrameFraction.note: A consequence of the framing rule and the subject, not a choice. The runner refuses a mismatch.
